history.heading: Kingdoms of the Senegambia
paragraphs: Senegal was part of the Ghana and Mali empires. The Jolof Empire, founded in the 13th century by the Wolof, dominated the region before splitting into kingdoms such as Kayor, Baol, Walo and Sine. The Tekrur kingdom in the Senegal River valley was one of the first in West Africa to adopt Islam.

history.heading: Slave trade and French colonisation
paragraphs: Portuguese traders arrived in the 15th century, followed by Dutch, British and French. Gorée Island became a symbolic site of the Atlantic slave trade and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. France founded Saint-Louis in 1659.

In the 19th century France conquered the interior, facing resistance from leaders such as Lat Dior. Senegal became the centre of French West Africa, with Dakar as its capital. Residents of the "Four Communes" gained French citizenship and elected deputies to the French parliament, such as Blaise Diagne in 1914. Senegalese soldiers (tirailleurs) fought for France in both world wars.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Senegal became independent on 20 August 1960, after a brief federation with Mali. Poet and statesman Léopold Sédar Senghor was the first president until 1980, when he voluntarily stepped down. Senegal is one of the few African countries never to have had a coup.

Abdoulaye Wade won in 2000, the first opposition victory. In 2024 opposition candidate Bassirou Diomaye Faye, released from prison just days before, won the presidency, with Ousmane Sonko as prime minister.

culture.heading: Teranga
paragraphs: Senegal is known for teranga, a Wolof word for hospitality. French is the official language, and Wolof is spoken by most people. About 95 percent are Muslim, and Sufi brotherhoods, such as the Mourides, founded by Cheikh Amadou Bamba, and the Tijaniyya are central to religious and social life; the Grand Magal pilgrimage to Touba draws millions.

Senghor was a founder of the Négritude movement. Musicians Youssou N'Dour and Baaba Maal are internationally famous, and mbalax is the popular music style. Thieboudienne (fish and rice) is recognised by UNESCO. Wrestling (laamb) and football are hugely popular; Senegal won the Africa Cup of Nations in 2022.

politics.heading: Democratic republic
paragraphs: Senegal is a presidential republic with a strong democratic tradition and peaceful transfers of power. The 2024 election followed a period of unrest when the previous president tried to postpone the vote. The new government promised to fight corruption and assert greater sovereignty, including the departure of French troops, completed in 2025.

economy.heading: Economic structure
paragraphs: Senegal's economy relies on services, agriculture (peanuts, millet and rice), fishing, phosphates, gold and remittances. Offshore oil and gas production began in 2024. In 2024 an audit revealed that public debt had been significantly understated, creating a debt challenge. The currency is the West African CFA franc.
